Study title: Outdoor Recreation Net Benefits of Rail-Trails
Calculation method: Individual travel cost method (ITCM): per-trip consumer surplus (CS) from a trip-demand model, scaled by annual visits
Equation of calculation method: CS per trip = integral of the demand curve above mean trip travel cost (Simpson's rule; -1/beta_TC for semi-log form). Total annual benefit = CS per trip x annual visits. Benefit per mile = Total / trail miles. Heritage: $30.18 (negative binomial) x 134,986 visits = $4,073,877; / 26 miles.
Statistical Distribution: Negative Binomial (also available: linear, self-logarithmic, robust, double-log, tobit)
CPI Notes: When using CPI Calculator, set January 1992 -> January 2024 (https://www.bls.gov/data/inflation_calculator.htm)
Uncertainty & assumption notes: Reported per-mile figure in the paper matches D/C. Per-trip CS varies widely by estimator (Heritage $21.83-$81.99; St. Marks $33.89-$112.31; Lafayette/Moraga $4.81-$19.48); the paper's headline choices are used here. Annual visits are visits, not unique users. Authors flag recall error in trip counts and omitted substitute-trail prices (possible CS overstatement at Lafayette/Moraga). Price year not stated in the text; wages were corrected to 1992 dollars (Smith 1983). Rural trail; mean one-way trip 34 miles, so mostly destination day-trips. Urbanicity from paper's trail-setting table.

Study title: Estimating the Economic Value and Impacts of Recreational Trails: A Case Study of the Virginia Creeper Rail Trail
Calculation method: Individual travel cost method (count-data models of annual trips, with and without travel-time opportunity cost); net economic value = consumer surplus
Equation of calculation method: CS per trip = -1/beta_TC. Aggregate net value = CS per trip x annual trips ($23-$38 per person per trip). Benefit per mile = Total / 34.
CPI Notes: When using CPI Calculator, set January 2003 -> January 2024 (https://www.bls.gov/data/inflation_calculator.htm)
Suggested Citation: Bowker, J. M., J.C. Bergstrom, J. Gill, 2007. “Estimating the economic value and impacts of recreational trails: a case study of the Virginia Creeper Rail Trail.” Tourism Economics. 13(2): 241-260.
Uncertainty & assumption notes: Midpoint of a reported range is my assumption; the paper reports no single point estimate. Users: 106,000 per the Headwaters summary, but a Forest Service newsletter cites ~130,000 annual visitors. Survey fielded 2002-03; price year not confirmed. 53% of visitors are nonlocal (avg ~260 miles one-way), so values reflect a destination trail and may exceed a purely local trail. Mileage 34 (some sources say 34.3). Only abstract/summary text reviewed, not the full paper.

Study title: A Contingent Trip Model for Estimating Rail-trail Demand
Calculation method: Contingent trip model (ex ante): mail survey of expected annual trips to a PROPOSED trail; negative binomial count model of trips vs. travel cost; consumer surplus
Equation of calculation method: CS per trip = -1/beta_TC (standard for semi-log count models; not verified in the paper). Total = CS per trip ($18.46-$29.23) x predicted annual household visits (416,213). Benefit per mile = Total / 23. Total entered is the reported lower bound ('in excess of $7.5M').
CPI Notes: When using CPI Calculator, set September 1999-> January 2024 (https://www.bls.gov/data/inflation_calculator.htm)
Suggested Citation: Betz, C., J. Bergstrom, and J.M. Bowker. 2003. “A contingent trip model for estimating rail-trail demand.” Journal of Environmental Planning and Management 46(1): 79-96.
Uncertainty & assumption notes: Total is a lower bound ('in excess of'). One summary says the study covers a SECTION of the proposed 23-mile trail, so the 23-mile divisor may overstate the mileage that was valued and understate per-mile value. Visits are predicted area-household visits (survey of residents within ~75 miles), not unique users. Stated (hypothetical) trips can be biased upward. Price year not stated in sources reviewed. Benefit per visit shown is the low end of $18.46-$29.23.

Study title: A Benefit-Cost Analysis of the Middle Fork Greenway Trail
Calculation method: Combined revealed + stated preference travel cost: panel Poisson (fixed effects, semi-log) on actual and hypothetical trips; benefit of added mileage
Equation of calculation method: CS per visit = -1/beta_TC. Total = N x deltaCS + deltaN x CS_with = 149,040 x $5.81 + 35,431 x $16.55 = $865,922 + $586,383 = $1,452,305 (first year of full completion). Benefit per added mile = Total / 6.5.
Uncertainty & assumption notes: Best fit for MARGINAL added-mileage value. Only 34 respondents; current annual visits (149,040) are a rough estimate from 28 hours of car counts (plausible range 12,960-285,120). Benefit is local residents' recreation only; excludes tourism spending. Survey 2011, paper January 2016; price year not stated. Net present value $2.78M (7%) / $7.36M (3%) vs ~$10M cost. Users shown = current annual visits (+35,431 new visits). Benefit/visit shown = CS with extension ($16.55); change = $5.81.
